seo.title: Rotate PDF – Turn Pages Permanently, Free & Private
seo.desc: Rotate PDF pages 90°, 180° or 270° and save permanently. All, odd, even, landscape-only or a page range. Batch files. Free, no upload, no sign-up.
sections: Fix sideways and upside-down pages for good

Scanners, phones and fax machines regularly produce PDFs with pages turned the wrong way: a landscape table lying on its side, a receipt upside down, every second page of a duplex scan rotated. Turning the page in your PDF viewer only changes the view on your screen – the next person who opens the file sees it sideways again. {brand} writes the new orientation into the PDF itself, so the file opens the right way up everywhere: in Acrobat, Chrome, Preview, on phones and when printed.

It runs entirely in your browser. The PDF is opened on your device, the page rotation is updated and the result is downloaded – nothing is uploaded, which matters for contracts, ID scans and medical letters.
Rotate exactly the pages you need
**All pages** – the classic fix for a whole document scanned the wrong way.
**Odd or even pages** – correct duplex scans where only the back sides are upside down.
**Landscape pages only / portrait pages only** – straighten mixed documents where only the wide tables or drawings are sideways.
**A page range** – type 2, 5-7 to turn just those pages.
**90° clockwise, 180° or 90° counter-clockwise** in one click.
**Batch** – drop several PDFs and get them all back rotated in one ZIP.
Lossless rotation

Rotation in a PDF is a property of each page. Changing it does not re-render or re-compress anything, so text stays selectable and searchable, links and form fields keep working, and images keep their full quality. The file size barely changes. This is different from tools that convert pages to images and back, which can blur text and bloat the file.
How to rotate a PDF
Drop one or more PDFs onto the page.
Choose the angle: 90° clockwise, 180° or 270° (90° counter-clockwise).
Choose which pages: all, odd, even, landscape, portrait or a range.
Click Rotate and download. The result tells you how many pages were turned.
Rotating on Mac, Windows and phones

On a Mac, Preview can rotate pages and save the change; on Windows, the free PDF readers generally only rotate the view. This tool works the same on every system, including Chromebooks, Android phones and iPhones, without installing anything. For individual pages that need different angles, use [Organize PDF](/organize-pdf/), where every thumbnail has its own rotate button.
Common uses
Straightening scanned contracts before e-mailing them.
Fixing landscape spreadsheets printed into a portrait report.
Correcting phone photos of documents converted with [JPG to PDF](/jpg-to-pdf/).
Preparing files for printing or for [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf/), so every page faces the same way.
Making scanned books readable on tablets.
Tips
If a page looks right in one viewer but wrong in another, the PDF may have an unusual rotation flag – rotating 360° (90° four times) normalises it.
Scanned pages that are slightly crooked (a few degrees) need straightening, not rotation – try [Deskew PDF](/deskew-pdf/).
Password-protected PDF? Open it with [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf/) first if you know the password.

seo.title: Protect PDF with Password – AES-256, Free, No Upload
seo.desc: Password-protect PDFs with AES-256 encryption. Control printing, copying and editing, set an owner password, batch files. Free, private, in your browser.
sections: Lock your PDF with strong encryption

A password-protected PDF can only be opened by someone who knows the password. {brand} encrypts your file with **AES-256**, the strongest standard PDF encryption and the default recommended by the current PDF specification (ISO 32000-2). Some popular online tools advertise AES-128; AES-256 is supported by every modern reader, including Adobe Acrobat, Chrome, Edge, Firefox, macOS Preview and mobile apps. If you must support very old software, you can switch to AES-128.
Encryption happens inside your browser. The unprotected document and the password never leave your device – there is no server that could log them, and nothing to delete after an hour.
Choose what readers may do
**Open password** – required to view the document at all.
**Allow printing** – untick to block printing in compliant readers.
**Allow copying** – untick to stop text and images being copied out.
**Allow editing** – untick to prevent changes and page reorganisation.
**Allow comments & form filling** – keep forms usable while locking everything else.
**Owner password** – a second password that unlocks the restrictions for you, while recipients keep the limited rights.
**Strength meter** – see instantly whether your password is weak or strong; generate one with our [Password Generator](/password-generator/).
**Batch** – protect several PDFs with the same settings and download a ZIP.
How PDF password protection works

When you protect a PDF, every text, image and font stream in the file is encrypted with a key derived from your password. Without the password the content is unreadable bytes. Permission settings (print, copy, edit) are stored alongside and honoured by standard PDF readers; they are a policy rather than unbreakable protection, so for truly confidential material rely on the open password and keep it secret.

Send the password through a different channel than the file – for example, the PDF by e-mail and the password by SMS or phone.
Store it in a password manager; a lost password cannot be recovered by anyone, including us.
How to password-protect a PDF
Drop your PDF (or several).
Type the password twice and check the strength indicator.
Optionally open Permissions to restrict printing, copying or editing and set an owner password.
Click Protect and download the encrypted PDF.
Common uses
Sending payslips, tax returns and bank statements by e-mail.
Sharing contracts and HR documents with candidates.
Distributing exam papers or answer keys.
Protecting client reports and medical records.
Locking finished e-books against easy copying.
Related tools

seo.title: Add Page Numbers to PDF – Free, Custom Format
seo.desc: Add page numbers to PDF: 6 positions, 'Page 1 of N', roman numerals, custom text, skip first pages, page range, facing pages. Free, no upload.
sections: Number your PDF pages exactly the way you need

Page numbers make long documents usable: readers can refer to 'page 14', printed copies can be put back in order, and tables of contents finally mean something. {brand} adds real text page numbers to any PDF in your browser – no upload, no watermark, no account. You decide where they go, what they look like and which pages get them.
All the options
**Six positions** – top or bottom, left, centre or right.
**Formats** – 1, 1 / N, Page 1, Page 1 of N, - 1 -, roman numerals (i, ii, iii) or completely custom text using {n} for the number and {N} for the total, e.g. 'Report 2026 – {n}/{N}'.
**Start number** – begin at 0, 1 or any number to continue the numbering of a previous volume.
**Skip first pages** – leave the cover and title page unnumbered; numbering starts after them.
**Page range** – number only, say, pages 3-20.
**Facing pages** – mirror left/right positions on even pages for printed, bound documents.
**Font, size, colour and margin** – Helvetica, Times, Courier or Helvetica Bold in any colour.
How to add page numbers to a PDF
Drop your PDF onto the page.
Choose a position and format, and set the starting number.
Open 'More options' to skip the cover, limit the range, change font, colour or margin, or enable facing pages.
Click Add page numbers and download. The result reports how many pages were numbered.
Which format should I use?

table: Page 1 of N, bottom centre or right
Custom text such as 'Exhibit A – {n}' (or use Bates numbering)

sections: Skipping the cover and numbering front matter separately

Academic and professional documents often number the preface with roman numerals and the main text with arabic numbers starting from 1. Do it in two passes: first number the front-matter pages with the roman format and a page range (e.g. 2-6); then run the tool again on the result with the arabic format, a range starting at the first chapter (e.g. 7-) and start number 1. Because both passes happen in your browser, this takes seconds.
Facing pages for printing

In a bound document, odd pages are on the right and even pages on the left. Numbers look best on the outer edge: right on odd pages, left on even pages. Tick **Facing pages** and choose a right-hand position – even pages automatically get the mirrored left position. This matches how professionally typeset books are numbered.
Why add numbers in the PDF rather than the source file?

Often you no longer have the Word or InDesign file, or the PDF is a combination of several sources – a scanned annex, a spreadsheet, a signed letter. After you [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf/) files together, adding numbers to the final PDF is the only way to get one continuous sequence. Numbers are added as real text, so they are searchable, print sharply and do not affect the rest of the page.
Legal numbering: Bates stamps

Law firms and courts often require Bates numbers – a prefix plus a zero-padded sequence such as ABC000123 – across all documents in a case. For that, use our dedicated [Bates numbering](/bates-numbering/) tool, which handles prefixes, suffixes and continuous numbering across many files.
Tips
Check the margin if your document already has a footer, so the numbers do not overlap it.
Use a grey colour for subtle numbers that do not distract from the content.
For headers and footers with dates, titles or other text, use [Header & Footer](/pdf-header-footer/).
Scanned pages? Numbers work the same way; run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) too if you want the document searchable.
Common uses
Numbering theses, dissertations and assignments to university requirements.
Preparing court bundles and exhibits.
Adding numbers to merged reports and board packs.
Numbering manuals, catalogues and printed booklets.
Making scanned archives easier to reference.

seo.title: OCR PDF – Make Scanned PDFs Searchable, Free
seo.desc: Turn scanned PDFs into searchable, copyable PDFs with free OCR in 12 languages incl. Hindi, Tamil, Arabic. Page range, TXT export. No upload.
sections: Make scans searchable and copyable

A scanned PDF is a stack of pictures: you cannot search it, copy a sentence from it or have a screen reader read it aloud. OCR (optical character recognition) reads the letters in those pictures and adds an invisible text layer exactly over them. The page looks the same, but now Ctrl+F finds words, text can be selected and copied, and the document can be indexed by your computer or a document management system.

{brand} runs OCR with the Tesseract engine inside your browser. The language models are downloaded once and cached; your scans are never uploaded. That makes it suitable for medical records, legal files, invoices and ID documents.
Features
**12 languages**, combinable two at a time – see the table below.
**Searchable PDF output** – original pages kept, invisible text added.
**TXT export** – get the recognised text as a plain-text file, or both PDF and TXT together.
**Page range** – OCR only the pages you need.
**Skip pages that already have text** – mixed documents are processed faster, and existing digital text is not duplicated.
**Adjustable resolution** – 200 DPI is a good default; raise it to 300 for small print.
Supported OCR languages

table: English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian

sections: Choose a second language for bilingual documents, such as English + Hindi or French + Arabic.
How to OCR a PDF
Drop your scanned PDF.
Choose the document's language (and optionally a second one).
Pick the output: searchable PDF, TXT, or both.
Optionally enter a page range and keep 'Skip pages that already contain text' ticked.
Click Start and wait – each page takes a few seconds depending on your device.
Download and test it: press Ctrl+F in your PDF reader and search for a word.
Getting the best accuracy
Scan at 300 DPI in greyscale or colour; 200 DPI is fine for normal-size print.
Straight pages recognise better – fix crooked scans with [Deskew PDF](/deskew-pdf/) and sideways pages with [Rotate PDF](/rotate-pdf/).
Choose the correct language; accents and non-Latin letters depend on it.
Very light, faded or handwritten text is hard for any OCR – handwriting is generally not supported.
For phone photos, [PDF Scanner](/pdf-scanner/) crops and enhances pages before OCR.
What can I do with an OCR'd PDF?
Search large archives of scanned letters and contracts.
Copy quotes and figures into reports.
Convert to editable formats with [PDF to Word](/pdf-to-word/) or tables with [PDF to Excel](/pdf-to-excel/).
Make documents accessible to screen-reader users.
Edit text with [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf/).
Searchable PDF vs text file

A searchable PDF keeps the exact look of the original scan with selectable text underneath – ideal for archives and sharing. A TXT file contains only the words, without layout – ideal for pasting into other programs, translation or analysis. Choose 'both' if you need each.
Privacy of OCR in the browser

Many online OCR services send your scans to a server for processing. Here, the OCR engine and language data run on your own computer or phone. Once the page and language model have loaded, you can even disconnect from the internet and keep processing.
Speed and large documents

OCR is computationally heavy. A modern laptop typically handles a page in a few seconds; phones take longer. For a 200-page scan, use the page range to process it in chunks, or leave the tab open while it works – progress is shown per page.
